label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Aligned framed wall modules and horizontal grille slots exist, but the shell contains only a floor and two walls, without a ceiling or complete returning enclosure. The rear-right dark feature is a plain slab without vertical patterning.

Both separate consoles have inclined faces, writing ledges and actual controls. However, the smaller console has only repeated dark controls and no framed light-faced instruments; its body is dark rather than the required light-gray or beige treatment. The oversized architectural shell also weakens the required proportional integration.

The yellow board has connected black branches, red circular lamps, amber square lamps and emissive assignments. Its selectors are plain cylinders without dial or tick scales. The simplified three-crossbar diagram and two FEHLERSTELLE labels do not provide the required reference-like interface distribution and detailed selector banks.

Neutral matte materials and broad area illumination keep equipment readable. However, the three thin fixture panels have no ceiling or mounting structure, so the required installed ceiling-mounted lighting system is incomplete.

Two distinct authored cameras exist, and the panorama axis points modestly downward. Nevertheless, the authored overview does not establish the required complete rectangular enclosure: the native shell lacks a ceiling and additional returning wall. No supplied render is identified as the second authored camera's close-up, so its detailed readability is not established.
The original final.png is a successfully decoded authentic PNG depicting this room, but its measured 374×512 dimensions fail the minimum 1920×1080 requirement.

The project opens and contains editable meshes, lights and two cameras. Cycles and view-layer denoising are saved, but the view transform is AgX rather than Filmic. All objects occupy the single master collection; named parent empties do not satisfy component-based collection organization.

dimension_scores.evidence: The long console, rear instrument arrays, grille, yellow board and smaller right console are recognizable, but their detail and architectural context are substantially simplified.

Console bases appear grounded and equipment is generally aligned. Overhead fixture strips appear unsupported, and the inclined console faces lack convincing enclosing support beneath their raised portions.
Muted cream-gray surfaces, dark bezels and the yellow board fit the requested palette. Blank instrument faces and repetitive controls reduce period-specific character.
Soft shadows provide depth, but blank gauges, primitive controls, sparse construction details and visible image noise make the room read as an early model.

The main equipment relationships are preserved: console forward, instrument bank behind, grille among the arrays and smaller console at right. Excessive empty room extent and incomplete enclosure weaken the spatial match.
The two consoles have plausible relative sizes and slopes, but the room is disproportionately expansive and tall compared with the equipment, and the wall meters appear coarse and oversized.
Diffuse neutral surfaces and soft illumination are appropriate and readable. Uniform material response, localized bright pools and substantial render grain limit the finish.
Major equipment assemblies are present, but the complete shell, patterned rear-right feature, gauge markings and detailed GRID selector interfaces are missing.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
